authority: User direction: useful OpenSearch-inspired partial compatibility; scalability governs API choices. Full compatibility is not a delivery requirement. Product requirements PR-01 to PR-54 (13 Nov 2026, docs/plan/product-requirements.md) extend rows A01 to A14 where they name an OpenSearch behaviour: refresh=true, _update, _reindex, by-query jobs, aliases, nested/join, PIT/scroll, real-time get, kNN, snapshots and extension modules. The fixture corpus under fixtures/api/core-v1 predates that revision and is refreshed by M06.05.
upstream_basis: Official OpenSearch latest documentation retrieved 2026-11-01. M02.01 must pin actual server/client versions and fixture hashes before any compatibility claim.

gates.measurement: Grow total idle catalog cardinality 10x while keeping selected partitions, dataset, concurrency and query fixed.
gates.pass: No full-catalog scan/timer/reader allocation; measured hot-request RSS and metadata attempts grow at most 10 percent, with repetitions/noise reported.

gates.measurement: Exceed every configured byte/count/deadline limit by one; include malformed NDJSON tail, oversized IDs and unsupported parameters.
gates.pass: Bounded typed refusal; structural bulk validation precedes commits; no unbounded allocation and no hidden successful write on a precommit refusal.

gates.measurement: Count total selected partitions separately from concurrent RPCs; include retries, cancellation, tenant skew and stalled peers.
gates.pass: Both configured limits and queue/remote-byte budgets hold; no retry outside the budget; an overloaded tenant cannot consume another tenant's reserved share.

gates.measurement: Page while indexing, deleting, splitting, moving readers, expiring snapshots and revoking keys.
gates.pass: No duplicate/omitted item within a valid snapshot and stable sort; exact generation or typed expiry/unavailability; quotas and GC pin invariants hold.

gates.measurement: Run high-cardinality buckets, bounded metrics, tie scores and approximate/limited total-hit cases against independent fixtures.
gates.pass: Never label incomplete counts exact; never silently truncate buckets; all advertised operator results and intentional differences match their declared oracle.

gates.measurement: M02.05 freezes matched workload/hardware/failure profiles and numerical thresholds using repeated component/single-node baselines; it does not qualify service scaling. M15.06 supplies real-provider profile curves. M17.03 repeats the implemented service at increasing worker counts, measuring latency, throughput, CPU/RSS, object attempts and directed network bytes.
gates.pass: Meet frozen per-profile minimum scale efficiency and latency/cost bounds; publish offered/completed/rejected load and curves. An unfrozen threshold, example limit or theoretical model cannot pass.

gates.measurement: Pin actual client/server versions and replay only the advertised profile, including error/timeout/idempotency and unsupported cases.
gates.pass: Only tested operations/versions earn compatibility claims; out-of-profile workloads receive an explicit adaptation report rather than a drop-in promise.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch provides dynamic mapping (true, false, strict), put-mapping for new fields, field, depth and nested limits, aliases with atomic actions, and rollover.
matrix.contract: Explicit versioned mappings with the supported field types. Per-index dynamic setting true, false or strict; a request that would pass the field limit (default from M02.05) is rejected whole, with nested depth and nested-object limits. New fields can be added online as a new immutable mapping version; changing an existing field's type or analyzer is refused. Identical canonical mappings share one stored object by content hash (PR-42, PR-43, PR-44). Aliases: one actions request is one atomic metadata change, so a request sees entirely the old target or entirely the new one; write aliases name one write index; rollover runs on request or an admitted check, never on a timer per index (PR-46, PR-34).
matrix.alternative: A type or analyzer change creates a new index and uses _reindex behind an alias swap (A03); unindexed source-only attributes remain retrievable, not searchable.
matrix.scalability: Field caps and content-hash sharing bound per-index metadata, so 10M indexes do not carry 10M mapping blobs, and sharing must never let one index read another's mapping. An alias swap costs a constant number of conditional writes, independent of index size.
matrix.acceptance: Field-limit, strict, false, per-item bulk error, concurrent add-field, type-change refusal and shared-hash isolation tests pass; reads and writes through an alias during a swap neither fail nor see a mix; an idle index with a rollover policy costs no requests.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch exposes ID-addressed document operations; GET is real-time by default; _update merges a partial document and supports upsert, doc_as_upsert, detect_noop and optimistic concurrency.
matrix.contract: Target familiar /{collection}/_doc/{id}, _update and _mget operations and core _id/_index/_source/found/result fields; initial mutations require an explicit stable document ID. GET is real-time: it returns the latest acknowledged write whether or not a reader covering it is published, from any coordinator, which forwards to the shard owner under an authority barrier shared by concurrent gets; realtime=false reads published state. Custom routing is honoured (PR-49). _update supports partial-document merge, upsert, doc_as_upsert, detect_noop and if_seq_no/if_primary_term; it is resolved once on the shard owner against committed state and the resolved operation is what is logged, so replay never re-evaluates it; scripts are excluded (A11) and it adds no object-store request beyond an index operation (PR-47). Exact response/client compatibility awaits fixtures.
matrix.alternative: Native /v1 document operations expose explicit receipts and read modes; read, change and index with a version token where an update mode is not offered.
matrix.scalability: Point requests route by logical identity; no stale fallback to make a get appear successful; barrier cost scales with shards and time, a multi-get costs requests by shards touched, and an update costs what an index operation costs.
matrix.acceptance: Create conflicts, missing deletes, lost replies, recreate/incarnation, read-after-write with refresh=false, owner kill, deposed-owner and lost-update-race histories pass; crash-replay of an update yields the same document.

matrix.surface: POST /_bulk NDJSON and bulk-shaped background jobs
matrix.upstream: OpenSearch actions are independent, item results are returned in submitted order, and index/create can generate an ID when omitted.
matrix.contract: Target index/create/delete with explicit stable IDs only; generated-ID modes are excluded from core-v1, and bulk update actions follow the _update contract in A02 once M21.06 passes. No cross-item transaction. Bodies are parsed as a stream under a configured buffer, with a document size limit and a hard ceiling of 200 MB (PR-16, PR-40); bounded whole-request structural validation precedes commits; item semantic failures do not erase other receipts. Preserve response item order and per-document mutation order. _reindex, update_by_query and delete_by_query are resumable, throttled, cancellable background jobs that read bounded pages from a pinned view and write through this bulk path, with progress reporting; a document changed since the pinned view is not overwritten or deleted blindly (PR-45, PR-48).
matrix.alternative: Large imports use bounded batches and resumable import jobs; retries use stable IDs/idempotency keys. Any later native allocated-ID profile must bound idempotency state and specify lost-reply recovery.
matrix.scalability: Explicit item/byte/response admission bounds buffering and fanout while retaining batching benefits; background job request cost follows bytes read and written, not documents matched, and jobs must not starve foreground traffic.
matrix.acceptance: Mixed success, repeated same-ID actions, omitted IDs, invalid tails, partial failures, uncertain acknowledgements, a 200 MB document and one byte over the limit are covered; job kill and resume loses and duplicates nothing and respects throttle and cancel.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch supports if_seq_no with if_primary_term and several versioning modes.
matrix.contract: Support if_seq_no with if_primary_term on index, delete and _update, mapped onto a native version that binds index, incarnation and document version, alongside the native opaque if_version token. Do not accept external/external_gte versioning modes (PR-47).
matrix.alternative: Read a native version token and submit a conditional replace/delete; external versioning is done by the client.
matrix.scalability: Logical version identity survives routing movement without exposing physical journal/group coordinates.
matrix.acceptance: Stale token, stale if_seq_no/if_primary_term, ABA recreation, split/move, duplicate retry and restore cannot overwrite a newer document.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch refresh=false, true and wait_for distinguish deferred visibility, forced refresh and waiting.
matrix.contract: All three modes are supported per request (PR-07). false acks when durable, wait_for acks when searchable, true acks once a reader covering the write is published and forces a publication if none is due, coalesced with other requests inside one batching window bounded by the profile and metered per index. A visibility timeout keeps the committed identity. Shard-copy-count durability parameters are excluded.
matrix.alternative: Use at_least(receipt) or a native visibility wait, and a versioned object/quorum durability profile. Maintenance is an admitted job, never per-write segment forcing.
matrix.scalability: refresh=true never costs one segment or object per write: concurrent forced refreshes share a publication, so request cost follows the window and not the writes. Never reduce accepted durability or misreport a committed write as rolled back.
matrix.acceptance: Each mode tested for ack semantics, timeout, lost replies and overload; 1,000 concurrent refresh=true writes cost publications set by the window; visibility p50 < 500 ms and p99 < 5 s measured under the declared load and reported as provisional.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch search_type can use shard-local or global term/document frequencies.
matrix.contract: Target match_all, term/terms, range, integer-threshold bool, match and match_phrase on declared fields/analyzer, bounded field sorting and source projection; nested and has_child/has_parent on fields mapped as nested or join, with parent and children routed to the same shard (PR-41); and kNN on fields mapped as knn_vector (HNSW and IVF, each with quantization and a disk-based variant, PR-22). Start with documented shard-local BM25; scores are not promised bit-identical across topology changes. Unknown operators/options fail, and a kNN query on a field that is not a knn_vector refuses.
matrix.alternative: Typed native query IR and capability discovery; global-statistics scoring is a later budgeted profile if justified.
matrix.scalability: Limits cover clauses, decoded data, candidates, total targets and concurrency. A stable snapshot/sort provides deterministic paging without universal score parity.
matrix.acceptance: Pinned analyzer/query golden cases and ranking tolerances are explicit; nested and join queries match pinned reference results on a shared corpus; recall@10 meets its floor for each vector variant; unsupported syntax cannot return empty success.

matrix.upstream: Deep from/size increases sorting/merge work; OpenSearch recommends PIT plus search_after, retains segment resources for PIT and scroll, and supports scroll for batch reads.
matrix.contract: from/size inside a configured window, search_after, PIT and scroll with OpenSearch request and response shapes, scroll served on the same pinned-view mechanism. A PIT or scroll pins an immutable per-shard view with a fixed routing and catalog generation (not one global instant), has a keep-alive, releases on request or expiry, and its pin is registered before the id is returned and honoured by garbage collection. Beyond-limit requests are rejected with the limit named (PR-54).
matrix.alternative: POST /v1/search-snapshots and cursor pages remain the native form; bulk export uses resumable jobs.
matrix.scalability: Separate total selected partitions from in-flight RPCs; enforce active-view and retained-byte quotas and show pins in metrics. Never expire a pin silently to serve newer data under an old id.
matrix.acceptance: Paging during writes, compaction, node kill, split, expiry, key revocation and GC gives no duplicate or gap within a view or a typed error; the window limit rejects from + size over the bound.

matrix.upstream: The Search API provides track_total_hits controls.
matrix.contract: Return exact counts only when evaluation completes within the admitted scope/budget; otherwise an explicitly requested lower-bound/limited result or a typed limit error. No mandatory unlimited exact count on every top-k request.
matrix.alternative: Budgeted count requests or resumable snapshot count jobs; relation/completeness fields state what was established.
matrix.scalability: Avoid coupling cheap top-k retrieval to unbounded full-scope counting.
matrix.acceptance: Threshold, missing partition and timeout cases never report an incomplete count as exact.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch terms can trade shard_size for accuracy; composite pages source-key-ordered buckets using after/after_key.
matrix.contract: Target bounded sum/min/max/value_count and finite bucket profiles. Exact terms require all necessary cardinality to fit the budget; otherwise refuse rather than silently truncate or invent an error bound. No universal aggregation-DSL compatibility.
matrix.alternative: Key-ordered snapshot group pages or admitted materialized views. Key order is not a substitute for global count-descending top-k.
matrix.scalability: Budget per-worker and coordinator buckets/bytes; asynchronous analytics handles work exceeding interactive limits.
matrix.acceptance: High cardinality, skew and ties distinguish exact, limited and unsupported outcomes using independent counts.

matrix.surface: Cross-shard joins and unsupported nested/join forms
matrix.upstream: OpenSearch documents has_child performance costs; nested objects are stored as additional Lucene documents.
matrix.contract: Nested and same-shard join support is in A06. Refused with a typed error: a join across shards, a child indexed without a routable parent, nested or join queries on fields not mapped as nested or join, and nesting beyond the configured depth and count (PR-41, PR-42).
matrix.alternative: Denormalized documents or bounded application-side lookups where a cross-shard join is needed.
matrix.scalability: Same-shard routing keeps a join local and avoids a fan-out; refusing a cross-shard join is a choice that avoids an unbounded fan-out, not a claim OpenSearch cannot join.
matrix.acceptance: Cross-shard join, child without routable parent and unmapped nested/join queries are rejected with a named reason and nothing is approximated.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch documents script queries as computationally expensive.
matrix.contract: No arbitrary per-document scripting or script-language compatibility in core-v1. Partial-document _update, upsert and detect_noop are supported without scripts (A02); a scripted update, a script query and unknown update options fail before any mutation. A sandboxed script form would need its own specification.
matrix.alternative: Typed client-side transforms and precomputed indexed fields; future bounded declarative transforms require replay determinism and CPU budgets.
matrix.scalability: Keep per-document CPU, replay and security costs predictable; exclusion is a product choice, not a claim that all scripts are unscalable.
matrix.acceptance: Scripts and unadvertised update modes refuse before mutation; replay never reexecutes nondeterministic user code.

matrix.surface: SQL/PPL, JVM plugins and queries on unmapped vector fields
matrix.upstream: OpenSearch SQL, PPL and Java plugins are outside the chosen core profile; no claim is made that they inherently cannot scale.
matrix.contract: No SQL or PPL and no JVM plugin compatibility. Extensions are native C-ABI shared libraries (in-process, trusted, strict version checks) or WASM modules (sandboxed, with memory, CPU and host-call limits), loaded by explicit node configuration per role, with no JVM and no scripting plugins (PR-23, D18). Vector search is in A06; a kNN query on a field that is not a knn_vector refuses.
matrix.alternative: Native modules for analyzers, query types, ingest processors and scoring functions; an out-of-process native module over a versioned RPC remains an optional third model; external analytics where appropriate.
matrix.scalability: Avoid turning OpenSearch's plugin ecosystem into a mandatory launch dependency. A native in-process module can take the node down, so it is enabled only by configuration; a WASM module that traps or exceeds its limits is stopped and the node keeps serving.
matrix.acceptance: Capabilities report absence of SQL/PPL and JVM plugins; an external example module loads as native and as WASM with identical results, a version mismatch is refused, and a disabled module is absent; unsupported workloads remain adaptation gaps, not silent substitutes.

matrix.upstream: OpenSearch exposes custom document routing and a Split Index API that creates a target index with more primary shards.
matrix.contract: Use stable logical partition keys and opaque routing generations; do not promise OpenSearch physical shard IDs/count settings, node pinning or split/shrink wire semantics.
matrix.alternative: Native topology policy, bounded paged catalog and online split/cutover jobs; routing hints never grant authority or replace tenant authorization.
matrix.scalability: Separate logical tenancy from active engines and physical journal groups, preserving hot-split flexibility and zero-idle control traffic.
matrix.acceptance: Stale routes, hot keys, split under load and 10x idle catalog growth preserve identity/fencing and resource bounds.

matrix.surface: _cluster/_cat settings, flush/force-merge and OpenSearch repository APIs
matrix.upstream: No compatibility is promised for another system's operational internals.
matrix.contract: Reject unadvertised cluster-manager, replica-count, maintenance and OpenSearch snapshot-repository APIs. Do not return fabricated shard/replica status fields. Snapshot and restore are native contracts (below), not the repository API.
matrix.alternative: Bounded authorized /v1 diagnostics, paginated catalog, per-role status and metrics, admitted maintenance, and native snapshots: a shallow snapshot is a metadata-only record that pins the index's immutable objects in the same store and restores same-key without copying, at a constant request count (PR-50); a full portable snapshot copies everything and restores on another provider as a resumable deep-copy job with its cost reported first (PR-51); export and cross-cluster copy serve independent indexes with their own key.
matrix.scalability: Avoid whole-cluster state responses and accidental all-partition maintenance storms.
matrix.acceptance: Unknown operational calls refuse; diagnostics and maintenance enforce scope, pagination and I/O budgets; snapshot request count is constant with index size, a pinned object is never collected, and a cross-provider restore returns identical results and survives deleting the source bucket.

matrix.upstream: This profile makes no comparative claim about OpenSearch cross-cluster implementation.
matrix.contract: No initial remote-cluster query syntax/semantics. Existing independent copy and CCR deliverables remain required optional modules.
matrix.alternative: Replicate/copy into a local read model; a future federation profile must price remote failure, latency and fanout separately.
matrix.scalability: Keep interactive authority, residency, latency and network budgets explicit rather than hiding remote work.
matrix.acceptance: Unsupported federation fails explicitly; copying/replication never weakens tenant/key or retention contracts.

matrix.upstream: Endpoint similarity alone does not establish client-version compatibility.
matrix.contract: Native /v1/capabilities lists implemented operations, limits and profile revision. Unknown parameters/operators return typed errors. Retain truthful item receipts, completeness and hsearch extensions instead of inventing OpenSearch internals.
matrix.alternative: A versioned thin adapter/SDK maps tested requests and documents required application changes; no universal drop-in claim.
matrix.scalability: Admission, deadline and unsupported outcomes are first-class; compatibility cannot hide unbounded work or silent degradation.
matrix.acceptance: Only runtime-tested features are advertised; unsupported and postcommit-timeout cases are in the client corpus.
